candidate.title: TruSeq RNA Stranded
candidate.scope: The single Illumina poster schematic titled TruSeq RNA Stranded, from supplied RNA through random-primed cDNA synthesis, dUTP-marked second-strand synthesis, grouped end preparation, adapter ligation, and selective amplification to an indexed directional DNA library ready for cluster generation. This is a product-level depiction with no kit revision specified and no alternative target workflow. Upstream RNA enrichment/fragmentation and downstream cluster generation or sequencing are not depicted.

states.label: Input RNA
features: Single RNA line drawn with 5′ at the left and 3′ at the right.
The schematic begins with RNA already supplied; its upstream selection and preparation are outside the depicted route.

features: Short blue primer drawn below the input RNA.

evidence.locator: Upper RNA, random-primer and Create cDNA panels; dTTP + dCTP + dATP + dGTP

states.label: Second-strand nucleotide mixture containing dUTP
features: Labeled dUTP + dCTP + dATP + dGTP; dUTP is highlighted.

states.label: Double-stranded cDNA with a uracil-marked second strand
features: Two DNA lines replace the RNA/cDNA depiction.
Repeated U symbols mark one strand, labeled Sense strand.
The first- and second-strand products are chemically distinguished by second-strand uracil incorporation.

evidence.locator: Create second strand cDNA arrow, dUTP nucleotide mixture and U-marked Sense strand

states.label: End-prepared, phosphorylated cDNA with A overhangs
features: The cDNA remains double stranded and retains the U-marked Sense strand.
Terminal P symbols are drawn at the upper left and lower right; A symbols are drawn at the opposite two ends.
These end modifications define the interface to adapter ligation; no separate intermediate for each end-treatment action is drawn.

evidence.locator: End repair / Phosphorylate / A-overhang panel; circled P and terminal A symbols

states.label: Adapter-ligated cDNA with uracil-marked second strand
features: Y-shaped adapter arms are covalently joined to both ends of the central cDNA insert, as represented by the ligation caption and continuous colored lines.
Adapter arms carry P5 and P7 labels together with Index 1 and Index 2.
The U-marked Sense strand persists through adapter ligation.

evidence.locator: Adaptor ligation arrow and Y-shaped adapter arms labeled P5, P7, Index 1 and Index 2

states.label: Uracil-marked second-strand template with blocked extension
features: The lower route in the Denature and amplify panel retains U marks and the Sense strand label.
A short extension at the right is annotated Block polymerase, contrasting with the complete amplified duplex above.
This is the blocked template route, excluded from the depicted final amplifiable product; its later physical removal or degradation is not shown.

evidence.locator: Denature and amplify panel; separated strands, U-marked Sense strand and Block polymerase label, then downward arrow

states.label: Directional indexed DNA library ready for cluster generation
features: Final library is represented by one continuous strand with P5 at the left, Index 2 near the left end, Index 1 near the right end, and P7 at the right.
The central insert is derived from RNA through cDNA synthesis.
The depicted final route has no U markings; the uracil-containing second-strand route is shown as blocked during amplification.
P5/P7 form the depicted cluster-generation interface; cluster formation and sequence measurement are not drawn.

evidence.locator: Bottom Product ready for cluster generation; linear P5 / Index 2 / insert / Index 1 / P7 product

evidence.rationale: Uracil is introduced specifically during second-strand synthesis; the figure subsequently marks this strand as blocked and retains the unmarked strand route in the final library. This supports strand-selective amplification at schematic scope, without specifying an enzyme or a sequencing-read convention.

operations.label: Create cDNA
operations.description: The random primer supports synthesis of a first DNA strand using the supplied RNA as template and the dTTP-containing nucleotide mixture. The output drawing retains the RNA alongside the new cDNA.
operations.mechanism: Random-primed RNA-to-cDNA synthesis is depicted; no enzyme identity is specified.
operations.information_effect: RNA sequence is represented in a DNA copy physically paired with its RNA template.

evidence.locator: Upper RNA, random-primer and Create cDNA panels; dTTP + dCTP + dATP + dGTP

operations.label: Create second strand cDNA
operations.description: The RNA/first-cDNA intermediate is converted into double-stranded cDNA. The newly depicted second strand incorporates U from the dUTP-containing mixture and is labeled Sense strand; RNA is no longer drawn in the output.
operations.mechanism: Second-strand DNA synthesis with dUTP in place of the first-step dTTP; no RNA-removal reaction is specified by the drawing.
operations.information_effect: The two DNA strands retain the RNA-derived insert sequence while the U-marked second strand records strand origin through a chemical distinction.

evidence.locator: Create second strand cDNA arrow, dUTP nucleotide mixture and U-marked Sense strand

operations.label: End repair / Phosphorylate / A-overhang
operations.description: The double-stranded cDNA ends are repaired, phosphorylated and given terminal A overhangs. The output preserves the uracil-marked strand and presents the modified ends for ligation. These actions are grouped because the figure supplies a single input/output boundary for them.
operations.mechanism: End repair, phosphorylation and A-overhang formation are explicitly named; specific enzymes and separate intermediate states are not shown.
operations.information_effect: The insert and strand marking are retained while the DNA termini are changed for adapter attachment.

evidence.locator: End repair / Phosphorylate / A-overhang panel; circled P and terminal A symbols

operations.label: Adaptor ligation
operations.description: Adapters are attached at both prepared cDNA ends, producing the depicted Y-ended construct with P5/P7 and Index 1/Index 2 regions. The U-containing strand remains present.
operations.mechanism: Ligation is explicitly labeled. The drawing shows the attached adapters, without a separate free-adapter reagent icon or a ligase identity.
operations.information_effect: RNA-derived insert DNA becomes physically linked to index regions and the P5/P7 sequencing-platform interface. No cell-level or molecule-level meaning for the indexes is specified.

evidence.locator: Adaptor ligation arrow and Y-shaped adapter arms labeled P5, P7, Index 1 and Index 2

operations.label: Denature and amplify
operations.description: The adapter-ligated strands separate and undergo amplification. The panel retains two strand routes: the unmarked strand yields a complete amplified duplex and the final P5-to-P7 library depiction, whereas the U-marked Sense strand is shown with a short extension and the Block polymerase annotation. The blocked route is retained as a separate material endpoint; no subsequent disposal step is depicted.
operations.mechanism: The figure depicts polymerase blocking associated with the uracil-containing strand. It does not name the polymerase or depict enzymatic excision or degradation of uracil-containing DNA.
operations.information_effect: Selective amplification retains strand-origin information in the RNA-derived DNA library. The final indexed DNA is the prospective sequencing carrier; this schematic does not specify a read-number-to-RNA-strand convention or show sequencing data.
